desc:
The array temps holds the temperature forecast for consecutive days. For each day i, find how many days you must wait to see a strictly warmer temperature than temps[i]. In other words, return an array answer where answer[i] is the smallest d > 0 such that temps[i + d] > temps[i], or 0 if no such day exists.

Example: temps = [73, 74, 75, 71, 69, 72, 76, 73] gives [1, 1, 4, 2, 1, 1, 0, 0].
hints: Scanning forward from every day is O(n<sup>2</sup>) in the worst case, for example for a steadily cooling forecast.
A day that has not yet found a warmer day is waiting. A new, warmer day settles all waiting days that are colder than it, and those days are the most recent waiting ones.
Keep a stack of waiting day indices, with temperatures non-increasing from bottom to top. For day i, pop every index j with temps[j] < temps[i] and set answer[j] = i - j; then push i.
editorial: This is the next greater element problem, asking for the distance instead of the value. Maintain a stack of indices of days that are still waiting for a warmer day. Temperatures on the stack never increase going up, because a warmer incoming day would have popped the colder ones.

When day i comes in, pop all indices j on top whose temperature is strictly lower than temps[i]; day i is the first warmer day for each of them (any earlier warmer day would already have popped them), so answer[j] = i - j. Push i. Days left on the stack at the end keep the answer 0. Each day is pushed and popped at most once: O(n) time, O(n) space.
